Here is the step-by-step calculation for the absolute pressure of the container at both locations.

The formula to calculate absolute pressure ($P_{abs}$) from gauge pressure ($P_{gauge}$) and atmospheric pressure ($P_{atm}$) is:
$$P_{abs} = P_{gauge} + P_{atm}$$

The gauge pressure of the container is **2.5 atm**.

---

### 1. Absolute Pressure at Sea Level

At sea level, the atmospheric pressure ($P_{atm}$) is **1 atm**.

$$P_{abs, sea\_level} = P_{gauge} + P_{atm, sea\_level}$$
$$P_{abs, sea\_level} = 2.5 \text{ atm} + 1 \text{ atm}$$
$$P_{abs, sea\_level} = 3.5 \text{ atm}$$

**The absolute pressure of the container at sea level will be 3.5 atm.**

---

### 2. Absolute Pressure at High Altitude

At the high-altitude location, the atmospheric pressure ($P_{atm}$) is **0.85 atm**.

$$P_{abs, high\_altitude} = P_{gauge} + P_{atm, high\_altitude}$$
$$P_{abs, high\_altitude} = 2.5 \text{ atm} + 0.85 \text{ atm}$$
$$P_{abs, high\_altitude} = 3.35 \text{ atm}$$

**The absolute pressure of the container at the high-altitude location will be 3.35 atm.**

---

### Summary

*   **Absolute pressure at sea level:** **3.5 atm**
*   **Absolute pressure at high altitude:** **3.35 atm**
